title: The Treasury sells 30-year bonds at 5.618 percent, the highest auction yield since 2000
dek: Bidders asked for two and a half times the amount on offer, at a price the government has not paid at a 30-year sale in a generation.
what: The Treasury sold $22 billion of 30-year bonds on Thursday at a high yield of 5.618 percent, the highest for a 30-year auction since August 2000. Bidders asked for 2.54 times the amount on offer. September's sale cleared at 5.308 percent and June's at 5.02 percent.
why: It is a clean, checkable record, the kind of number market accounts post the minute it prints.
